summary: Round-3: all three round-2 blockers genuinely closed and verified against code. Contract ok, 31/31 verify green. Approve with three non-blocking stale-count doc nits.
notes: contract-check ok=true, zero violations; not_checked: forbid.behaviors (evaluated by hand below). acceptance-coverage status=pass, zero gaps, AC-1..AC-6 all covered. 05-validation.json overall_result=passed, 31/31 commands exit 0.

ROUND-2 BLOCKER 1 (pools-doc-no-afirmar-cobertura-inexistente) CLOSED. crates/hexcell-storage/src/pools.rs:421-432 no longer claims coverage that did not exist: it names la_copia_conserva_la_epoca_fijada_aunque_el_enlace_vivo_ya_apunte_a_la_siguiente, the test that actually exercises the window, and states the mutation result. That claim matches the orchestrator's independent M5 run exactly (forcing verificar_copia to report the live epoch fails only that test, exit 101).

ROUND-2 BLOCKER 2 (h1-copia-sobre-el-pool-superseido) CLOSED. The third test is sound, not merely green. Verified by construction, not by trusting the prose: (a) the spin in esperar_a_que_el_respaldo_tome_una_celda_de_conocimiento reads gestor.conocimiento().lecturas_en_reposo(), which try_locks every cell of the LIVE KNOWLEDGE pool only (pools.rs:225-235). The test retains no cell, the promotion thread has not started, and setup (promover_y_drenar_epoca_inicial, sembrar_staging_marcado) completed synchronously before the spawn, so a false can only come from the backup. (b) respaldar_en reaches the knowledge pool via self.conocimiento.load().con_lectura(...) AFTER the sessions.db copy, so observing a held cell proves the arc_swap Guard was already pinned to the epoch-1 pool, whose SQLite fds are bound to the epoch-1 inode; repointing the symlink afterwards cannot change which file the copy reads. (c) Loop exhaustion panics with an explicit message (no silent pass); VUELTAS_MAXIMAS_DE_ESPERA=50_000_000 yields, so exhaustion is a loud failure, never a false green.

On the AtomicBool: it proves the respaldar_en CALL had not returned, not literally that VACUUM INTO was mid-flight - the knowledge copy is the last operation before a Vec construction, so the gap is a few instructions. This is not load-bearing. Soundness rests on the Guard pinning established by the spin plus three independent content-based assertions (6000 EPOCA-UNO / 0 EPOCA-DOS markers, metadatos_de_epoca row = 1, reported field = 1) against the counterfactual that canonicalize(knowledge_live.db) already resolves to knowledge_epoch_2.db. The overlap assertion is a correct belt-and-braces guard against the degenerate zero-overlap run.

MERGE-IMPOSSIBILITY CONFIRMED: the two overlap tests genuinely require opposite orderings, not merely different ones. Test 1 brakes the SINGLE sessions.db read connection, which respaldar_en copies FIRST, so the switchover necessarily completes before the knowledge copy begins (knowledge copy = epoch 2). Test 3 has no brake and its spin requires the backup to be INSIDE the knowledge con_lectura before promotion starts (knowledge copy = epoch 1). One run cannot have the knowledge copy both start after and span the switchover. Neither can silently degrade into the other: test 1's brake is deterministic (one connection), test 3's spin panics if the window is never observed, and both assert the AtomicBool.

ROUND-2 BLOCKER 3 (adr-0031-corregir-la-afirmacion-de-inalcanzabilidad) CLOSED. Every rewritten factual claim checked against code, given HEX-061 shipped an inverted comparison that only review caught. Decision 5-ter's three reasons braking is unreachable all hold: retaining all cells stalls the promotion too (promocion.rs:460-462, pool_anterior.con_lectura before the swap); retaining one stalls nobody because pools.rs:176 is siguiente.fetch_add(1, Relaxed) % len, so with width 2 the next caller provably gets the other cell; and width 1 would hang promover_epoca WITH THE LINK ALREADY REPOINTED - correct precisely because reasignar_enlace_de_la_epoca_viva (promocion.rs:451) precedes pool_anterior.con_lectura (promocion.rs:461). No inversion this round.

Decision 4's reconciliation with decision 6 is also accurate: drenaje.rs:206 tests epoca.instante_de_reemplazo().elapsed() >= limite BEFORE the sleep at drenaje.rs:214, so a 1 ms limit expires on the first loop turn without ever sleeping the 5 ms INTERVALO_DE_SONDEO_DE_DRENAJE. The ADR now says openly that poll repetition is NOT exercised, which is the honest statement.

BITACORA IMMUTABILITY CONFIRMED: the branch-wide diff of docs/bitacora-de-descartes.md contains only the header date line, four added index rows (D-35, D-36, D-37, D-38) and the appended D-38 body. The bodies of D-35 (line 530), D-36 (542) and D-37 (550) are byte-identical to main - the index rows were recovered without touching the entries. D-38 (558) is intact with its discard reason and reopening condition.

INVARIANTS INTACT: Cargo.toml untouched (no new deps); hexcell-core dependency-free (cargo tree = 1 line); no tokio/async/.await in hexcell-storage; no std::env::set_var or remove_var; D-33 held (no --test-threads=1, no serial_test); adr-0028 and NFR-03 CI guards still present and greppable (estres_conmutacion_veinte_lecturas_concurrentes, duracion_de_conmutacion_ms); ADR numbering sequential with adr-0031 appended and no existing row rewritten; all dates absolute; all content Spanish; no AI attribution in any of c37d995, a4d47b1, 96a839b.

NIT 1 (non-blocking, stale count): docs/adr/README.md:42 - the adr-0031 index row still summarises the ADR as 'dos pruebas #[ignore] ejecutadas por nombre en CI'. There are now three. The ADR body itself was corrected to 'las tres pruebas'; only the index row lags. Number, title, stage and date are correct, so ADR numbering authority is unaffected.

NIT 2 (non-blocking, stale count): docs/STATUS.md:24 - the HEX-062 entry says 'con dos pruebas #[ignore] ejecutadas por nombre desde dos pasos dedicados' and enumerates only (1) and (2), omitting the third test entirely. Everything it asserts about (1) and (2) is true; it is incomplete rather than wrong, and the normative record (adr-0031) and ci.yml are both correct and complete.

NIT 3 (non-blocking, stale count): .github/workflows/ci.yml:49 - the block comment above the steps still reads 'Sin estos dos pasos especificos'; there are now three steps. The third step itself (ci.yml:63-66 region) exists, is correctly named and carries its own explanatory comment.

NOT a defect - checked and cleared: tests/respaldo_durante_conmutacion.rs:22 says 'las dos pruebas concurrentes de este archivo' in the context of the AtomicBool overlap assertion. That is accurate: exactly two of the three tests assert overlap that way (H3 does not).

CI-STABILITY OBSERVATION (not a correctness defect): the third test's overlap assertion depends on the promotion (~2 ms measured) finishing inside the knowledge copy (~28 ms measured), a ~15x margin. On a saturated 2-core runner an inversion would produce a false FAILURE, never a false pass, so the failure mode is fail-loud. The ADR states honestly that the 6000-fragment seeding makes the case reachable and proves nothing by itself.

THIRD CONTRACT AMENDMENT - JUDGEMENT: defensible engineering, but only just, and it should not recur. In its favour: the touch/forbid file set never widened (11/11 files across all three rounds, zero violations), src/** stayed well inside its caps (hexcell-storage/src 94/120, hexcell/src 7/40) and was untouched by the last two amendments, so no scope crept into production code; and the final increment was compelled by review findings, which is the one legitimate reason to raise a cap mid-flight - a limit that forbids the fix review demanded is a limit fighting its own purpose. Against it: three successive raises of the same limit, each after the diff had already exceeded it, means the cap never once acted as a brake - it functioned as a ratchet. The recorded reason (blueprint sized 480 against a real ~895 because it mis-modelled comment density in a concurrency test) is a genuine sizing diagnosis rather than a rationalisation, and it is the right lesson to keep.

AMENDMENT - DESCRIBE VS CONSTRAIN: the final numbers describe more than they constrain. 895/920 in hexcell-storage/tests leaves 25 lines of headroom (97.3% consumed); a cap that only forbids a 26th line is a record of what was delivered, not a boundary that shaped it. Global 1137/1260 is looser at 90%. The real fence that held this task was the file list, not the line count. Recommend q-memory capture the blueprint-sizing lesson: comment-dense concurrency tests in this repo run roughly 2x a naive line estimate.

forbid.behaviors evaluated by hand (the automatic check does not cover it): no executor introduced, no environment mutation, no test-suite serialisation, no mutual exclusion added between backup and promotion, no weakening of the NFR-03 or adr-0028 guards, no rewriting of existing ADR rows or bitacora bodies. All clear.
